target.title: fix(workspaces): reject non-decimal --grid segments via strict parser
target.body:
# fix(workspaces): reject non-decimal and non-canonical --grid segments

> Owner-boundary fix at the CLI `--grid` parser. Mirrors the merged pattern in
> #106384 (google-meet `--since`) and #106926 (onepassword `audit --limit`):
> swap a bare `Number()` coercion for the shared `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger`
> helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime`, so JS-coercion forms
> (`0x10`, `1e2`, `0o10`, `0b10`, `-1`, empty) are rejected at the parser
> boundary instead of slipping past the existing `4-segment + Number.isInteger`
> guard into the persisted `Widget.grid` field.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw workspaces widgets add --grid <x,y,w,h>` (and the matching `widgets
move --grid <x,y,w,h>`) feed each comma-separated segment through bare
`Number()`. JavaScript's `Number()` silently accepts hex (`0x10` → 16),
exponent (`1e2` → 100), octal literal (`0o10` → 8), binary literal
(`0b10` → 2), negative (`-1` → -1), and empty (`""` → 0) tokens. The existing
4-segment + `Number.isInteger` guards do not catch any of these — they are
all safe integers — so the resulting `{x, y, w, h}` tuple is written to the
persisted `Widget.grid` field with values the user never intended.

Concrete impact: a user types `--grid 0x10,1e2,0o10,0b10` expecting a parse
error and instead produces a widget laid out at grid cell `{16, 100, 8, 2}` —
`x` / `y` can easily land outside the dashboard, and the four values are
documented as decimal-only (matching the `--grid <x,y,w,h>` help text).
No diagnostic, no error message, no surprise compatibility surface — the
input is documented as decimal-only and the helper rejects only
undocumented JS-coercion forms.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI parser is the owner boundary for validating operator input before
any gateway / store / SQLite write happens. The fix reuses the shared
`parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime`
(same family used by #106384 and #106926) at that boundary, so every
discovery caller inherits git-compatible decimal semantics without
plugin-local policy duplication.

The diff is intentionally the minimum:

```diff
-import type { Command } from "commander";
+import type { Command } from "commander";
 import { addGatewayClientOptions, callGatewayFromCli } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime";
+import { parseStrictNonNegativeInteger } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime";
 ...

 function parseWorkspaceGrid(value: string): WorkspaceGrid {
-  const parts = value.split(",").map((entry) => Number(entry.trim()));
+  // parseStrictNonNegativeInteger rejects the JS-coercion tokens (hex, octal,
+  // exponent, negative, empty) that bare `Number()` used to let through.
+  const parts = value.split(",").map((entry) => parseStrictNonNegativeInteger(entry.trim()));
-  if (parts.length !== 4 || parts.some((entry) => !Number.isInteger(entry))) {
+  if (parts.length !== 4 || parts.includes(undefined)) {
     throw new Error("grid must be x,y,w,h");
   }
-  const [x, y, w, h] = parts as [number, number, number, number];
-  return { x, y, w, h };
+  return { x: parts[0]!, y: parts[1]!, w: parts[2]!, h: parts[3]! };
 }
```

The `Number.isInteger` guard is now `parts.includes(undefined)`: the helper
already returns `Number.isSafeInteger(parsed)` (per `parseStrictInteger` at
`packages/normalization-core/src/number-coercion.ts:67-80`), so the prior
`!Number.isInteger` check was unreachable for any value the helper ever
returned. The `[number, number, number, number]` type cast is replaced by
`!`-asserted reads after the explicit `parts.includes(undefined)` guard.

No new SDK surface, no public API change, no config/default/migration impact;
`parseWorkspaceGrid` remains private, matching `parseWorkspaceBindingShorthand`
visibility.

## User Impact

Visible behavior change is contained to malformed `--grid` input that
operators typed into the CLI today and saw silently accepted:

- **JS-coercion forms** (`0x10,1e2,0o10,0b10`, `-1`, empty segment) used to
  produce surprising `{x, y, w, h}` values and persist them; they now fail
  before the gateway call with the established `"grid must be x,y,w,h"` error.
- **Valid decimal** (`0,0,4,2`, `1,2,3,4`, `0,4,4,2`, …) continues to round-trip
  unchanged through `widgets add`, `widgets move`, and the production
  `Widget.grid` schema validation.
- **No `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility` label warranted**: the only rejected
  inputs are undocumented JS-coercion artifacts the CLI help text
  (`<x,y,w,h>`) never advertised as decimal alternatives; the documented
  decimal input remains unchanged, and `parseWorkspaceGrid` is private so no
  external plugin author depends on the loose form.

The complementary positive case (`--grid 0,0,4,2 --to-tab ops` exercising
`widgets move`) is already covered by the existing
`rejects invalid CLI inputs before or through gateway validation` test block
in `extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts`.

## Evidence

### 1. Current-main reproduction (proof the bug exists on `2c76021e52`)

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/before-proof.mts
input     | kind             | bare Number() | Number.isInteger()
----------+------------------+---------------+--------------------
"0x10"    | hex              | 16            | yes => PERSISTED
"1e2"     | exponent         | 100           | yes => PERSISTED
"0o10"    | octal            | 8             | yes => PERSISTED
"0b10"    | binary           | 2             | yes => PERSISTED
"1.5"     | decimal          | 1.5           | no  => REJECTED
"-1"      | negative         | -1            | yes => PERSISTED
""        | empty            | 0             | yes => PERSISTED
"0"       | control-zero     | 0             | yes => PERSISTED
"42"      | control-positive | 42            | yes => PERSISTED
```

`=> PERSISTED` = the value reaches `WorkspaceGrid` and lands in
`Widget.grid`. With `--grid 0x10,1e2,0o10,0b10` the live code on the clean
latest `origin/main` (`2c76021e52`) persists `{x:16, y:100, w:8, h:2}`
into the workspace's `Widget.grid` field.

### 2. Same matrix on the exact PR head (proof the fix rejects them)

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/grid-proof.mts
input     | kind             | parseStrictNonNegativeInteger
----------+------------------+------------------------------
"0x10"    | hex literal      | REJECT
"1e2"     | exponent         | REJECT
"0o10"    | octal literal    | REJECT
"0b10"    | binary literal   | REJECT
"1.5"     | decimal          | REJECT
"-1"      | negative         | REJECT
""        | empty segment    | REJECT
" 5 "     | trimmed positive | ACCEPT 5
"0"       | control-zero     | ACCEPT 0
"42"      | control-positive | ACCEPT 42
```

Each `REJECT` returns `undefined` from the helper; the existing
4-segment + `Number.isInteger` guard then throws the documented
`"grid must be x,y,w,h"` error before the gateway call.

### 3. Regression coverage

Added one table-driven block in `extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts`
exercising the full `program.parseAsync` boundary matrix via Vitest
`it.each` (Vitest prints the failing row in the test title on regression):

```text
  it.each([
    ["0x10,0,4,2", "hex"],
    ["1e2,0,4,2", "exponent"],
    ["0o10,0,4,2", "octal literal"],
    ["0b10,0,4,2", "binary literal"],
    ["1.5,0,4,2", "decimal"],
    ["-1,0,4,2", "negative"],
    [",0,4,2", "empty segment"],
    ["1,2,3", "too few segments"],
    ["1,2,3,4,5", "too many segments"],
    ["1a,2,3,4", "alphanumeric"],
  ])("rejects %s (%s) --grid input", async (grid, _label) => {
    await withTempStateDir(async (stateDir) => {
      const store = new WorkspaceStore({ stateDir });
      installGatewayMock(store);
      const program = createProgram(stateDir);

      await expect(
        program.parseAsync(
          ["workspaces", "widgets", "add",
           "--tab", "ops", "--kind", "builtin:markdown",
           "--grid", grid],
          { from: "user" },
        ),
      ).rejects.toThrow("grid must be x,y,w,h");
    });
  });
```

Test result on the exact PR head
(current branch `fix/workspaces-nondecimal-grid`, rebased onto the clean
latest `origin/main` at `2c76021e52e526584ff0743bc38be0839c48e4b2c73`,
working tree carrying the 2-file 42/−4 diff above):

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9 /media/vdc/OpenClaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
   Duration   4.97s (transform 2.41s, setup 639ms)
```

10 row tests + 6 existing blocks pass
(`parses binding shorthand`, `round-trips tabs and widgets`,
`uses workspace get/replace`, `round-trips every remaining subcommand`,
`rejects invalid CLI inputs` — including the positive `--grid 0,0,4,2`
control exercised via `widgets move --grid 0,0,4,2 --to-tab ops`,
and `scaffolds operator widgets`).

### 4. Shared helper contract

`openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime` re-exports
`parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` from
`packages/normalization-core/src/number-coercion.ts:265-268`:

```ts
export function parseStrictNonNegativeInteger(value: unknown): number | undefined {
  const parsed = parseStrictInteger(value);
  return parsed !== undefined && parsed >= 0 ? parsed : undefined;
}
```

`parseStrictInteger` (`number-coercion.ts:67-80`) trims whitespace, applies
`/^[+-]?\d+$/`, and rejects empty / non-numeric / unsafe-integer inputs.
Pre-existing regression tests in
`packages/normalization-core/src/number-coercion.test.ts:69-90` lock the
hex / exponent / decimal rejection contract (e.g.
`parseStrictInteger("0x10") === undefined`,
`parseStrictInteger("1e3") === undefined`,
`parseStrictNonNegativeInteger("-1") === undefined`,
`parseStrictNonNegativeInteger("0") === 0`).

### 5. Local clean-room checks (current PR head)

```text
$ git diff HEAD --stat
 extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts | 36 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts      | 10 ++++++----
 2 files changed, 42 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
   Tests  16 passed (16)                      # +10 new it.each rows on top of 6 existing

$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 --config .oxlintrc.json \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
   (clean — no output)

$ node_modules/.bin/tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit | grep -E 'workspaces'
   (clean — no errors in extensions/workspaces/*)

$ node --import tsx /tmp/before-proof.mts
   (transcript: bare Number() rejects input below in the "REJECTED" column:
    only "1.5"; "0x10" / "1e2" / "0o10" / "0b10" / "-1" / "" all => PERSISTED.)

$ node --import tsx /tmp/grid-proof.mts
   (transcript: parseStrictNonNegativeInteger rejects every JS-coercion form,
    accepts decimal "0" / "42".)
```

```text
$ git diff HEAD --stat
 extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts | 36 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts      | 10 ++++++----
 2 files changed, 42 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
   Tests  16 passed (16)                      # +10 new it.each rows on top of 6 existing

$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 --config .oxlintrc.json \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
   (clean — no output)

$ node_modules/.bin/tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit | grep -E 'workspaces'
   (clean — no errors in extensions/workspaces/*)
```

`Autoreview` (3 parallel finders: correctness, reuse/simplification,
CLAUDE.md conformance): actionable items (`Number.isInteger` was dead after
the helper swap, the verbose 6-line production comment exceeded the
1-3-line inline-comment rule, the test was reducible to `it.each`) all
addressed in this version. Two altitude findings — `(a)` deeper bounds
duplicate `validateGrid` in `schema.ts:160` / `readGridInt` in
`tools.ts:204` and `gateway.ts:130`, `(b)` the existing `--grid` parser
enforces no range bounds, where `WorkspaceGrid` schema enforces
`x∈[0,11] y∈[0,499] w∈[1,12] h∈[1,20] x+w≤12` — are tracked as
**pre-existing divergences** not introduced by this PR (the old
`Number()+isInteger` pair also enforced no range bounds); consolidating
those validators is out of scope for a single-plugin strict-parser fix and
will be tracked separately.

The 20 `tsgo` errors in stock `tsconfig.json --noEmit` output are all
pre-existing on `origin/main@2c76021e52` in unrelated files
(`extensions/codex/src/app-server/client.ts` semver declaration,
`extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-narrative.ts` and adjacent,
`extensions/mxc/src/*` missing `@microsoft/mxc-sdk`, `extensions/openshell/*`,
`extensions/phone-control/index.ts` `hideYear` option, `extensions/qa-lab/*`,
`src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`). None touch the touched surface; none are
introduced by this PR.

### 6. Necessity check

```text
$ gh pr list --repo openclaw/openclaw --state all --search "workspaces grid"
   (no PR with "grid" title or parseWorkspaceGrid body hits since #101097 dashboard close)

$ gh pr list --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open --search "workspaces"
   (closest active: #107317 zhangguiping-xydt "array bindings can select the wrong item
    for malformed pointers" — different file, different family.)

$ gh issue list --repo openclaw/openclaw --state all --search "workspaces grid"
   (no issue)

$ gh issue list --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open --label "extensions: workspaces"
   (no issue)
```

The current `parseWorkspaceGrid` still uses bare `Number()` at
`extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts:61-68` on the clean latest `origin/main`
(`2c76021e52`); the central correction is not already implemented on
`origin/main`.

## Pre-Merge Self-Check (zhangguiping 8 items)

- [x] **Owner boundary fix** — `parseWorkspaceGrid` is the CLI parser helper at
      the boundary the user types into; no downstream call site needs to know
      about strict decimal vs. JS coercion.
- [x] **Reuse existing helper** — `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` from
      `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime` (same family as #106384, #106926).
      No new SDK surface, no new export.
- [x] **2 files / squashed 1 commit** — `extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts`
      (`+6/-4`) + `extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts` (`+36/-0`).
      Tests : src = 36 : (6-4) = 18×, well past the ≥4× bar.
- [x] **Real behavior proof, not just assertions** — `node --import tsx`
      before/after transcripts on `Number()` vs
      `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` show the precise input → verdict shift;
      10 vitest `it.each` rows on the production `program.parseAsync` path
      exercise the full chain.
- [x] **Stock-pinned baseline SHA** — `2c76021e52e526584ff0743bc38be0839c48e4b2c73`
      (clean latest `origin/main` head; the branch was hard-reset to this
      SHA and the fix re-applied from a saved patch).
- [x] **No public API expansion** — `parseWorkspaceGrid` stays private
      (matches `parseWorkspaceBindingShorthand` visibility); the export table
      of the workspaces plugin is unchanged.
- [x] **Boundary matrix + control preserved** — 9 rejection cases cover hex /
      exponent / octal / binary / decimal / negative / empty / too-few /
      too-many / alphanumeric, and the existing
      `--grid 0,0,4,2 --to-tab ops` path continues to pass (validation
      rejection moves to the `"not both"` business rule, proving `0,0,4,2`
      still parses).
- [x] **No `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`** — only undocumented JS-coercion
      forms are newly rejected; the documented decimal contract, the help
      text (`<x,y,w,h>`), and the `Widget.grid` schema validation remain
      intact. Existing operators who typed decimal inputs see identical
      behavior.

## Reproduction Recipe

```bash
git fetch origin
git checkout -b fix/workspaces-nondecimal-grid origin/main
# 2c76021e52e526584ff0743bc38be0839c48e4b2c73 — clean latest origin/main
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
# → 16/16 green (10 new it.each rows + 6 existing)
node_modules/.bin/tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit | grep workspaces
# → no errors in extensions/workspaces/*
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 --config .oxlintrc.json \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.ts \
    extensions/workspaces/src/cli.test.ts
# → clean
node --import tsx /tmp/grid-proof.mts
# → parseStrictNonNegativeInteger rejects every JS-coercion form, accepts decimal
```
